title: Custom domains
standfirst: Putting an agent behind your own hostname is a feature some providers sell, some leave to a proxy you run, and several do not offer at all.
idea: A custom domain is an HTTPS hostname you control, pointed at a port inside the sandbox. It matters when the URL is the product: a client-facing demo, a webhook receiver, or an agent whose address should not be a provider subdomain that changes.

There are three levels. Native: the provider issues a certificate for your hostname and routes it. Do-it-yourself: the provider gives you a stable hostname and you put your own proxy in front. Absent: no documented path, and the preview URL is what you have.
The differences are in the details: whether you can delegate a subdomain or must move a whole domain's nameservers, whether certificates are automatic, and whether the domain survives a resume.

splits.heading: Native, self-serve domains
body: Runtime routes a sandbox's web port at your hostname with HTTPS. boxd lets you point one domain at a machine or delegate a wildcard subdomain to the whole organisation, and issues certificates automatically. Blaxel's preview URLs support optional auth and custom domains.

quote.text: boxd verifies your DNS and issues TLS certificates automatically.

splits.heading: Do it yourself, or not at all
body: Sandboxer calls first-class custom domains a roadmap item and documents a CNAME plus your own TLS termination. E2B's guide sets up a customer-operated GCP VM running Caddy and Cloudflare DNS to proxy requests to the sandbox. Boat explicitly does not support custom domains.

quote.text: We will set up a GCP VM running Caddy server with Docker and Cloudflare DNS to proxy the requests to the Sandboxes.

splits.heading: Not published is not the same as no
body: InstaBox, Morph, Sprites and Vercel Sandbox publish no sandbox custom-domain feature. Vercel has domains for deployments, which is a different product; Sprites has organisation-private URLs; InstaBox has public ports only. For these, the honest answer is that the research found nothing either way.

watchFor: Whether you must move a whole domain's nameservers or can delegate one subdomain.
Whether the certificate is issued automatically.
Whether the domain survives a stop and resume, or must be re-pointed.
Whether the feature is native or a proxy you operate.
Whether the domain is for sandboxes or only for deployed apps.

rows.note: Custom domains are supported, but only by delegating a whole dedicated domain's nameservers; a subdomain of an existing domain cannot be registered.

rows.note: No custom-domain feature appears in the docs or the API. Public ports on the provider's hostname are the only inbound path.
Custom domains are documented for deployed app services, not for sandbox preview URLs. A sandbox preview stays on the provider's hostname.
No custom-domain feature is documented for instances or devboxes. An HTTP service can be exposed, but the hostname is the provider's.
A sandbox's web port can run at your own hostname with HTTPS, verified by DNS records and a certificate from Let's Encrypt.

source.quote: **Custom domain:** a sandbox's web port at your own hostname, with HTTPS.

rows.note: First-class custom domains are on the roadmap; the documented workaround is a CNAME to the hosted hostname with your own TLS termination.
